purpose: Turn RC29's conceptual 1,530-unit design into machine-checkable evidence, trace, reference, revocation, and denominator contracts before any hardware enrollment or hidden-vendor result exists.

standardsBoundary.rfc9999: The envelope uses the finalized RFC 9999 application/cmw+json media type and explicit conceptual-message indicator semantics.
standardsBoundary.rfc9711: Evidence claim names and freshness semantics are EAT-compatible research choices, not a registered EAT profile.
standardsBoundary.rfc9943: Trace statements, receipts, and transparency roles are SCITT-aligned, but no production transparency service or cryptographic receipt is implemented.
standardsBoundary.corim: Reference and authority semantics are inspired by draft-ietf-rats-corim-11, which was an active Internet-Draft on the review date; the JSON registry is not CoRIM conformance.
standardsBoundary.hardwareAttestation: Physical property, context, Measurement Unit, and Target Environment fields track draft-paka-rats-hardware-component-attestation-00, an early work in progress.
standardsBoundary.jsonSchema: Five structural contracts use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. Cross-document time ordering, digest equality, uniqueness, and statistical scope are semantic gates outside JSON Schema.

sealedTimeline.rule: Every policy, reference, exclusion, denominator, and nuisance-correction digest must be fixed before hiddenVendorRevealedAt. Any later mutation invalidates performance adjudication rather than merely lowering confidence.

hiddenVendorDesign.rule: In each prospective hardware fold, one entire vendor and all its process-lot cells remain unavailable to threshold fitting, nuisance fitting, reference construction, and attack-family selection.
hiddenVendorDesign.syntheticScope: RC30 uses a single synthetic hidden-vendor bundle to falsify the contract. It does not estimate transport performance.

hypotheses.claim: Five Draft 2020-12 schemas are sufficient to adjudicate the complete protocol.
hypotheses.prediction: Every semantically invalid mutation must fail schema validation.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any mutation passes all structural schemas but fails a cross-document semantic gate.

hypotheses.claim: A policy digest alone proves that policy was frozen before hidden-vendor reveal.
hypotheses.prediction: A post-reveal policy with a self-consistent new digest must be accepted.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The chronology gate rejects a self-consistent policy whose frozenAt is at or after reveal.

hypotheses.claim: A 1,530-row ledger is a valid denominator whenever its row count is correct.
hypotheses.prediction: Duplicating a unit or replacing one physical package with a rerun leaves the claim valid.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Unique physical-unit and cell-balance gates reject the row-count-preserving mutation.

hypotheses.claim: A structurally and semantically valid bundle proves hidden-vendor hardware performance.
hypotheses.prediction: Contract passage is sufficient to claim a one-percent bound on VENDOR-GAMMA.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The adjudicator reports protocol-readiness only because no physical device or independent institution was tested.

independentAdjudication.developmentArtifacts: Schemas, generator, synthetic vendor identities, thresholds, mutation catalogue, and JavaScript semantic verifier in this repository.
independentAdjudication.independentAudit: A Python implementation reconstructs chronology, digest, ledger, balance, and mutation outcomes without executing or importing the JavaScript runner.
independentAdjudication.futureHardwareAdjudication: A separate institution must create its own parser and verifier from the frozen schemas, receive unseen vendors and units, and retain ground truth until all appraisal outputs are committed.

securitySafetyPrivacy.operationalBoundary: No secret extraction, invasive package modification, live-supply-chain interference, bypass technique, production key, or customer record is included.
securitySafetyPrivacy.testAuthority: Real adversarial fixtures require written ownership or authorization, controlled handling, safety review, partner approval, and coordinated disclosure.
securitySafetyPrivacy.dataMinimization: Public records use synthetic vendor codes and package identifiers. Real lot, customer, location, personnel, and commercially sensitive provenance remain access-controlled.
securitySafetyPrivacy.parserRisk: Implementations must bound CMW nesting, reject unknown critical fields, cap input size, and avoid automatic decoding of embedded content.

nonClaims: No EAT profile registration, CoRIM conformance, SCITT service operation, or production cryptographic protection is established.
No package, chiplet, PUF, PDN sensor, vendor, lot, fab, attacker, or independent institution is measured.
No false-accept, false-reject, transport, cell-specific, or hardware-security rate is estimated.
Passing a schema proves only constraints explicitly represented by that schema.
